subject: Prod readiness: serving lane preference & rollback/rollover plan
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@greenfieldhealth.com>, Greenfield Procurement <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's call — deployment lanes and migration constraints

Thanks Jonas — good call this morning. A couple of clarifications from our infra team: we currently run two production stacks that will need to be supported during cutover:

- An internal self-hosted cluster ("LegacyGPU") with a custom KV cache and a slightly different tokenization pipeline (byte-level tokenizer).
- Traffic coming from an existing third-party LLM API provider (we'll call them OtherLLM), which is used by a handful of services and can't be changed overnight.

Short answers we need to proceed with procurement: can Redwood support a staged migration where:
1) We begin with Hosted for our internal-facing feature flags (low-volume) while we validate answers and latency.
2) Move a mid-volume customer-facing path to Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and to test the KV cache sync and tokenization parity.
3) Final cutover to Private VPC for HIPAA-sensitive endpoints once SOC2 and HSM integration work is complete.

Also: what is the expected window for a rollback if we fail traffic validation from Dedicated to LegacyGPU? Do you have a recommended rollback cadence or an automated fallback policy? We want a concrete plan in the next 72 hours to share with procurement and our CTO.

Thanks,
Lina
Director, Platform Engineering
Greenfield Health

[attachment: gf_po_prelim.pdf (application/pdf, 87KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's call — deployment lanes and migration constraints

Lina — thanks for the clear summary. Short version: yes, the staged plan you outlined is supported and is what we recommend for customers with mixed legacy and security needs. Below is a concise runbook and the immediate asks so your procurement/CTO can sign off quickly.

Runbook (high level):
- Phase 0: Pilot (Hosted) — 2 weeks
  - Use Hosted API with isolated API key for internal traffic. Validates tokenization/semantics against your golden prompt set.
  - Goal: detect tokenization drift and basic latency profile.

- Phase 1: Dedicated validation — 3–4 weeks
  - Provision Dedicated capacity sized to your p50/p95 targets (attached estimator).
  - Run mirrored traffic for a small percentage (5–10%). Enable KL-based quality checks and KV-cache sync validation.
  - Failure mode: automatic routing back to OtherLLM or LegacyGPU based on policy.

- Phase 2: Private VPC cutover — 4–6 weeks
  - Bring up Private control plane, HSM/KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence. Gradual traffic ramp to 100%.
  - Post-cutover: optional warm standby Dedicated for fast rollback.

Rollback and fallback specifics:
- Automated fallback: Redwood can route requests to a compatible model variant or a configured external endpoint (OtherLLM) when health checks fail.
- Rollback window: we recommend a warm-standby Dedicated or keep a short-term replica of LegacyGPU for a minimum of 72 hours during initial cutover. That gives you a deterministic path back if regressions appear.
- Decision gates: quality regressions (KL > 0.12 on key prompts), latency breach (p95 > agreed SLA), or error-rate spike (>1%).

Immediate asks from us to finalize sizing and SOW:
1) Golden prompt set (5–10 prompts representative of high-risk flows) — provide by EOD Thu (2026-11-05).
2) Typical batch sizes / max sequence length for the services hitting the API.
3) Desired p95 latency and cost sensitivity (low/medium/high).
4) Procurement point-of-contact for contract terms and any required IP addenda.

I attached the Dedicated sizing worksheet and a SOC2 snapshot. Marissa will follow up on HSM/KMS integration details. If you want, we can lock a 30-minute deep dive this Thursday with our infra lead to walk through KV cache sync patterns and tokenization mismatches.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical check Thu 2026-11-05 10:00 PT — does that work?

—Jonas
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx, soc2-snapshot-2026.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@greenfieldhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's call — deployment lanes and migration constraints

Hi Lina — quick technical clarifications from my side (infra ops):

- Tokenization: we can run a tokenization parity check against a sample of your corpus. If byte-level differences are the main cause of drift we can add a small preprocessing shim in Dedicated or Private to normalize tokens before inference.
- KV cache: Redwood supports export/import of KV cache snapshots and has APIs to stream deltas. For a staged migration we typically do an initial full snapshot from LegacyGPU and then periodic deltas for the first 48–72 hours.
- Metrics & tracing: we will provide per-request latency traces and token-level cost breakdown so you can correlate regressions to model behavior.

Two quick asks for sizing: please confirm whether your max sequence length is typically <= 1,024 tokens or if you have longer (2,048+) sessions. That materially changes Dedicated instance class. Also, do you need guaranteed GPU affinity for KV-intensive workloads?

I'll join the technical check on Thu if scheduled.

—Marissa
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[No attachments]

From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@greenfieldhealth.com>, Greenfield Procurement <procurement@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's call — deployment lanes and migration constraints

Thanks team — appreciate the clarity. A few procurement/ops notes from my side:

- Procurement needs the initial SOW and estimated monthly committed spend for Dedicated (ballpark numbers are fine) to start internal approvals.
- We will aim to deliver the golden prompt set and typical batch sizes by Thu EOD.
- For rollback appetite: CTO wants a 24–48 hour hard rollback guarantee for any customer-facing path in Phase 1; is that feasible if we maintain a warm standby?

Can you send a simple table with the minimal Dedicated configuration that meets p95 <= 300ms and p95 <= 150ms (two rows), with estimated monthly costs and an expected timeline to spin up? Procurement needs that to match budget windows.

I'll confirm the attendees for the Thu deep dive once we have the time locked.

Thanks,
Carlos
VP, Infrastructure
Greenfield Health
